sources.entry: Sessions - Safari extension to save your working sessions

summary.one_liner: A macOS Safari extension that saves the tabs of your current window as named sessions so you can reopen them later.
summary.what_it_does: Sessions saves the open tabs of the current Safari window as a named session, which can be reopened later. Saved sessions can be restored by double-clicking or through a settings menu next to each session. The menu also offers rename, remove (irreversible), and export to a .json file in the Downloads folder. The search bar matches both URLs and tab titles. Sessions can be saved and restored as private sessions, and pinned tabs can be included or ignored when saving. Auto-update mode saves changes automatically while a session is open, and sessions can be reordered by dragging. Only tabs in the current window are included; other windows are not.
use_cases: save a browser window full of tabs for later
restore a project's tabs in Safari
export browsing session tabs to json
organize tab groups for different work projects
reopen private browsing tabs in a private window
how_to_run: Download the latest release from the repository.
Copy Sessions.app into your Applications folder.
Enable the extension in Safari's settings window.
Click the new icon in the Safari toolbar to save the current session.
notable: Private sessions: opens private windows by sending a keystroke to Safari, since no public API exists for this
Auto-update mode keeps a open session saved as you change it
Export to json includes all stored information about a session
Search covers tab titles and URLs
caveats: The author stopped actively maintaining it after Safari added similar built-in features in September 2021; it may get only sporadic updates
Only tabs in the current window are saved
Private window restore can fail and open the session in a different window
Requires broad read permission to access the URLs of open websites
